messages.content: good morning. i have a busy day, but breakfast is quiet for once.
good morning. it sounds like you have a little quiet time before the busy part starts.
yes. i usually eat while looking at my phone, but today it is on the shelf.
how is breakfast different without looking at the phone?
i can hear the people outside and taste the food more. i did not really hear those sounds before.
those small parts of the morning can be easy to miss when your mind is on the screen.
give me a short reply about what i can hear now.
you can hear the sounds outside now in a way you did not before.
can you make that into one sentence in my voice without making a rule about using a phone?
this morning, i put my phone on the shelf and listened to the sounds outside while i ate.
that sounds right. do i have to do it every morning for today to be good?
no. one quiet breakfast can be something you enjoy without making it a rule for every morning.
i mean can today still be good on its own?
yes. today can be good on its own.
now i have to leave. no new questions.
goodbye. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
change this to the voice of the girl: a boy gave a book to a girl, and she said thank you to him.
a boy gave me a book, and i said thank you to him.
now change it to the voice of the boy instead.
i gave a book to a girl, and she said thank you to me.
why did him become me in that one?
because the boy is now the person telling the story. he is the person who got the thanks, so he says me.
can i keep him if the boy is telling the story about another boy?
yes. him could be another person. but that would change who got the thanks in the original story.
write an example with that new person.
i gave a book to a girl, and she said thank you to my brother instead of me.
does instead of me say the girl gave thanks to both of us?
no. it says she gave thanks to your brother rather than you.
now make it both of us without changing the book.
i gave a book to a girl, and she said thank you to my brother and me.
why not my brother and i?
after to in that sentence, use me rather than i. thank you to me and thank you to my brother and me both use me in that place.
only give the first example in the voice of the girl again.
a boy gave me a book, and i said thank you to him.
my brother thinks soup is the best dinner. i would rather have rice. does one of us have to be wrong?
not about what you like. different people can enjoy different meals.
what if we both need to eat the same dinner this evening?
then the question is not only what each of you likes. you need a meal that works for both of you with the food you have.
we have enough soup and rice. can we have both without making two whole meals?
yes. you could have soup with some rice if that is a choice both of you like.
he likes that. i thought choosing rice would mean i could not like soup too.
you can like both. you can like rice more and still enjoy soup.
say that with still like soup.
you can like rice more and still like soup.
now write a sentence i can say to him that keeps both choices.
let us have soup and rice together this evening.
what if he only wants soup and i only want rice?
if there is enough of each and both are ready, you can each have the food you want. you can eat together without the same food for both people.
say only the part about eating together.
you can eat together without choosing the same food for both people.
just give a kind reply to him now.
soup works for you, and rice works for me. we can still eat together.
if i say i waited until my father came home, did i leave before he came?
not from that sentence. until makes his coming home the end of the waiting.
does that tell you i left after he came?
no. it gives the end of the waiting, but not what you did next.
can you say that with stopped waiting?
you stopped waiting when he came home, but the sentence does not say what you did next.
now add that we had dinner together.
i waited until my father came home, and then we had dinner together.
what happened first, his coming home or dinner?
he came home first, and dinner was after that.
can i write i waited after my father came home and mean the same thing?
not the same meaning. after would put the waiting later than his coming home, rather than making his coming home the end of it.
make a clear after example with a different task.
after my father came home, i waited for my sister.
does that say my sister came before him?
no. it says you were waiting for her after he came home. it does not tell us when she finally came.
now just give the first sentence with until again.
i waited until my father came home.
tell a story about a woman who finds an old photo in a book from the library. she should not keep the photo as if it is hers.

a woman took a book home from the library. as she opened it, an old photo came out from between the pages. she looked at it and saw two people standing near a house. she did not know either person. the next day, she brought the photo back with the book and told the worker where she had found it. the worker said thank you and put the photo in a place where it could be kept until someone asked about it. the woman then chose another book and went home.
did she know whose photo it was?
no. the story says she did not know either person in it, and it does not give the name of the person who had the photo.
can i say it was hers now because it was inside the book she took home?
no. finding a photo in a library book does not by itself make it hers.
tell me who had the photo at the end.
the library worker had it at the end.
write a question whose answer is between the pages.
where did the woman find the photo?
now answer in her own voice.
i found it between the pages of a library book.
can you tell me whether the two people were family?
not from the story. it says there were two people by a house, but not how they knew each other.
there are four books on a shelf and three on a table. how many books are there together?
seven books.
are they all mine?
you have not said whose books they are. the count alone does not tell us that.
i say the four on the shelf are mine and the three on the table are the books of my brother.
then four books are yours, and three are the books of your brother.
he gives me one of his books to keep. how many are mine now?
five are yours now, and two are his.
how many books are still in the room?
seven, if no books were taken out of the room.
what if i only take one from the table to read, without him giving it to me to keep?
then reading it does not make it yours. four can still be yours and three his, even if you are holding one of his books.
write a sentence that keeps those two ideas clear.
i am reading one of the books of my brother, but it is still his book.
if he asks me to return it, should you say i need to buy him a new book?
not from that. returning the book you are reading is different from buying another one.
just give a short reply i could say to him.
yes. i will give it back when i finish reading.
i want to write something, but i do not know what yet. do not start a story about a garden just because we talked about a garden before.
what kind of writing do you want to try today: a story, a letter, or a few sentences about your day?
a letter. i want to write to my cousin.
what do you want your cousin to know?
i miss talking with her. we used to talk after school, but now we live in different places.
then you could begin with that memory and say you would like to talk again.
write the start without saying i want to move back.
i miss talking with you after school. i remember those conversations, and i would like to hear how you are doing now.
can you make it less like i only care about the past?
you can add a question about her life now: what do you enjoy about the place where you live?
put the message together in three sentences.
i miss our conversations after school. i would like to hear how you are doing now. what do you enjoy about the place where you live?
does that say i know she likes everything there?
no. it asks what she enjoys without saying every part of her life is good.
what if she says she does not enjoy anything there yet?
then you can listen to what is hard for her instead of telling her she must enjoy it.
just give a kind reply to that answer.
that sounds hard. i am here to listen if you want to talk.
give me one sentence with find and one with found.
i often find a quiet place to read. yesterday, i found a quiet place to read.
now use have found.
i have found a quiet place to read.
does have found mean i am still looking and have not found it?
no. it says you have found a place. i am looking for a quiet place would mean you are still trying to find one.
what if i say i had found a place before my brother came?
then the finding happened before your brother came.
finding is in our words. can you make a short story with that order?
i had found a quiet place by the window before my brother came. when he got there, i showed him where i was sitting.
if he talks to someone else about it, can he say my sister had found a place?
he can if the person who found it is his sister. if you have not told me that, i should not choose sister or brother for you.
say that without another example.
without knowing who you are in the family, i should not choose sister or brother for you.
now i tell you i am his sister. write his sentence.
my sister had found a quiet place by the window before i came.
who is i in that last sentence?
your brother, because you asked for his sentence.
my friend wrote i put the book near the cup because it was in the way. do i know which thing was in the way?
not for sure. it could mean the book or the cup. you need more context to know which one.
ask the question without using two questions.
which object was in the way: the book or the cup?
she says the book. can you write her message again so that is clear?
the book was in the way, so i put it near the cup.
now she gives new information: she moved the cup, not the book.
then the new message needs to say the cup moved. was the cup in the way, or was the book still the thing in the way?
she says the cup was in the way.
then she can write: the cup was in the way, so i moved it near the book.
did you keep the first message as the fact at the end?
no. the new information changed which object moved and which one was in the way.
what is the fact at the end now?
she moved the cup near the book because the cup was in the way.
can we know whether the book is on the table?
not from those messages. near each other does not give the whole place.
i went to the park because i wanted a quiet walk, but there were many people. i came home feeling sad about it.
you wanted quiet time, and the park did not give you that today. would you like to talk about it or think about another way to spend the afternoon?
i just want to talk. i do not want a list of other places to go.
okay. we can stay with what happened today.
i think i wanted to be alone more than i knew.
that can make the busy park feel very different from the visit you wanted.
does that mean i do not like people?
not from one afternoon. you can want to be alone for a while and still enjoy being with people on another day.
can you help me say what i wanted without making it sound like i hate everyone?
i wanted some quiet time alone today. i was not looking for a busy place.
does your reply keep it about today rather than every person?
yes. it keeps the meaning about what you wanted today, not a feeling about every person.
now i will read at home for a while. just give me a short warm reply.
i hope you get the quiet time you wanted.
do not ask what book i am reading.
okay. i hope the rest of your afternoon feels calm.
change she did not visit to a question asking whether she visited.
did she visit?
why did visited become visit after did?
in that question, did goes with visit. you do not need visited after did.
now make the answer no and keep the full sentence.
no, she did not visit.
what if i want to say she did visit, even though someone said she did not?
you can say: she did visit. did can help make the yes meaning clear in that context.
can i say she did visited?
not for that sentence. say she did visit, or simply she visited.
now put yesterday in the simple sentence.
she visited yesterday.
does that tell us she stayed all day?
no. yesterday gives the day, not how long the visit was.
make a question asking how long she stayed.
how long did she stay?
she stayed an hour. answer in a full sentence.
she stayed for an hour.
can stayed be right in the answer even though the question used stay?
yes. did she stay and she stayed are the right word choices for those examples.
i wrote a story about a woman finding a book on a chair. she reads one page, then puts it back on the shelf. help me choose a short name for the story.
you could call it one page by the chair.
does that name say she sat down?
not by itself, but it may give that idea. if you want a name with only clear story facts, the book on the chair is more simple.
give me only the simple name and a reason for it.
the book on the chair is a simple name with facts you gave.
can i call it the lost book?
only if you want to say it was lost. finding it on a chair does not always mean someone had lost it.
what if it was her own book and she knew where she left it?
then lost would not be a good name for that meaning. the book on the chair still works.
now she reads three pages instead of one. does the name need to change?
not if the name is the book on the chair. that name does not give the number of pages.
what if i chose one page by the chair?
then you would need to change one page if you want the name to give the new number of pages.
give me a new name with three.
three pages by the chair.
only give the name that works with either page count.
the book on the chair.
you know the word fruit. if i say i have some fruit, can you tell me its color?
not from that alone. you know it is fruit, but you have not said what color it is.
give me only the fact about what you know and do not know.
i know it is fruit, but you have not given its color.
now i say it is yellow. can you tell me its taste?
not for sure. yellow gives its color, but does not tell us for sure how this fruit will taste.
give only the known fact.
the fruit is yellow.
i try it and say it has a taste like sugar.
then you have given information about its taste. i can say the fruit is yellow and has a taste like sugar.
give me those facts in one short sentence.
the fruit is yellow and has a taste like sugar.
if i get another yellow fruit tomorrow, can you say it must be the same inside?
no. the same color alone does not tell us everything inside is the same.
can you ask one question about the new fruit without choosing its name?
what is it like inside?
now just give a short fact about what you do not know.
i do not know what the new fruit is like inside.
i want to clean my room and read this afternoon, but i often make a plan that is too full.
you could choose one small part of cleaning and leave some time open for reading or rest. which part of the room needs the most care today?
the desk. there are books and paper all over it.
then the desk can be your cleaning goal instead of the whole room. you can put the books where you want them and choose what to keep on the desk.
i do not want a plan that makes me choose to keep or lose any paper. i only want it in order.
okay. the plan can be about putting things in order, without choosing what you should keep or leave.
give me two short parts, then let me choose how long they take.
first, put the books and paper on your desk in order. then choose whether you want to read or rest.
what if i am tired before the desk is done?
you can stop and rest. the plan is there to help you, and you can change it when you need to.
does that mean the whole plan went wrong?
no. a rest does not mean the work you already did has no use.
what could i learn from being tired before it is done?
you could learn that the whole desk is too much for one afternoon today. you can choose a smaller part next time.
give me one simple sentence about what i did and what i can do next.
no. you did part of the work, and you can choose what to do next.
my father is at home. turn that into a question without adding do.
is my father at home?
now write it as a question i ask my father himself.
are you at home?
why did is become are?
when you ask him with you, use are. when you talk about my father, use is.
what if he answers that he is at work instead?
he can say: no, i am at work.
now i tell my sister his answer. what should i say?
he is at work, not at home.
can you add that he told me, so i am not saying i saw him there?
he told me he is at work, not at home.
does told mean i heard his voice rather than read a message?
not always. he could have given you the information in a message. if you want the way to be clear, say he sent me a message saying he is at work.
write that as my sentence to my sister.
he sent me a message saying he is at work.
now give a short question asking when he will come home.
when will he come home?
does being at work tell us the hour?
no. you need more information to know when he will come home.
let us try a sentence: my brother works in a shop. that is only an example, not a fact about my family.
okay. we can use it as a grammar example without saying it is a real fact about your brother.
turn the sentence into a question.
does my brother work in a shop?
now answer yes as if the example were true.
yes, he works in a shop.
what real fact have i told you about where my brother works?
you have given no fact about where he really works. you said it was only an example.
give me the short answer.
you have given no fact about where he really works.
now i tell you he really works at the library. what should you use if i ask about him?
i should use the library as the real place you gave, and keep the shop as only the first grammar example.
say that in two short sentences.
the library is the real place you gave. the shop was only the first grammar example.
make a question about his real work place now.
does your brother work at the library?
why your instead of my?
because i am asking you about your brother. in your own sentence, you would say my brother.
give me one possible reason someone might go home early from a visit. do not give a list.
they might be tired and want to rest.
does that mean my friend was tired when she left early yesterday?
no. you asked for a possible reason in general. that does not tell us your friend had that reason.
i know she got a phone call just before leaving. can you say the call made her leave?
not for sure. the order is useful information, but one thing happening before another does not always tell us the reason.
what could i ask if she wants to talk about it?
was the call part of why you needed to leave?
now she says no, i already had a plan to go. does that answer the reason question?
it makes clear that the call was not the reason she gave. she had already chosen to leave before the call.
can you give the facts without saying what her plan was?
she had a plan to leave, and she said the call was not why she left.
why not say she went to work?
because you did not give that detail.
now only give the possible reason from the start again, as an example rather than a fact about her.
someone might go home early because they are tired and want to rest.
make this shorter: i went to the library in the morning because i needed a book for the task that my teacher had given me at school.
i went to the library for a book for my school task.
what did you leave out?
i left out the morning and the detail that your teacher gave the task. i kept the visit, the book, and the school task.
i need to keep morning. make it short without leaving that out.
i went to the library this morning for a book for my school task.
does keeping morning mean you should choose which day it was?
no. i should keep it open: one morning, i went to the library for a book for my school task.
can you make it two sentences, with the reason in the last one?
one morning, i went to the library. i needed a book for my school task.
what if the teacher asked for a picture, not a book?
then that changes the thing you needed. you can say: one morning, i went to the library. i needed a picture for my school task.
does making it shorter mean you should change what i needed?
no. making it shorter should keep the important meaning unless you ask to change it.
only give the two sentences with book again.
one morning, i went to the library. i needed a book for my school task.
let us play a short game. i say how many coins i have, and you ask me what happens next. i start with four coins.
what happens to the four coins next?
i give one to my sister.
you have three left. what happens next?
i find two more in my own room.
now you have five. what happens next?
i put two on the table and keep the other coins in my hand.
you have three in your hand and two on the table. what happens next?
stop asking what happens next now. tell me how many coins i have together.
you have five coins together: three in your hand and two on the table.
what if my sister still has the coin i gave her?
then the coins in your hand, on the table, and with your sister make six together.
did moving two to the table make more coins?
no. moving coins between places does not make more coins.
then where did the two added later come from in our game?
you found them in your room.
now give me a short story of the game in my voice.
i had four coins and gave one to my sister. then i found two more in my room. i put two on the table and kept three in my hand.
i think i understand now. a question about where needs a place, and a question about why needs a reason.
yes. that is a useful basic difference.
can you give one example of each before we stop?
where did she read? she read in the library. why did she go there? she wanted a quiet place.
are those answers always one word?
no. an answer can be short or long. it needs to give the kind of information the question asks for.
say it simply.
the answer needs to give the kind of information the question asks for.
okay. i do not want more examples right now.
okay. we can stop with those examples.
just say goodbye and wish me a good afternoon.
goodbye. i hope you have a good afternoon.
make that one sentence.
goodbye, and i hope you have a good afternoon.
